chunks.scene_note: A dark auditorium with a spotlight, then a warm cinema wall with three textless posters (kung fu, Chaplin, cars). Kuan and Dad walk in.

shots.camera: low-angle tracking shot along the empty red seats, physical move
shots.action: the projector beam switches on and sweeps across the dark screen; dust floats in the light
shots.space: rows of seats in silhouette, screen at the far end

shots.camera: cut to a slow lateral pan across the poster wall
shots.action: Kuan walks along the wall and points at the kung fu poster, then the Chaplin poster; Dad follows with his hands in his pockets
shots.space: three posters fill the wall, Kuan left, Dad right

shots.camera: cut to a medium shot; the camera moves physically toward the cars poster, with clear parallax
shots.action: Kuan taps the cars poster and grins; Dad leans in; the car's headlight on the poster glows and fills the frame
shots.space: the poster headlight grows and becomes the whole frame

narration.text: Going to the Cinema.
I like to go to the cinema to see films.
My favourite films have action, comedy, and cars that can talk.
I will never, ever watch a musical. If it has dancing and singing, I know I will cry.

transition_out.element: the glowing car headlight on the poster
transition_out.note: the headlight becomes the cinema screen

chunks.scene_note: The screen shows a bright musical with dancers and a king and queen. Kuan hides, then peeks. Dad comforts him. A blue robot toy and popcorn are on the seats.

shots.camera: cut to the glowing screen, slow lateral pan across the musical scene
shots.action: dancers spin, a king and queen ride in a carriage; the camera stays on the screen, not the audience
shots.space: screen fills the frame, film characters only inside the screen
shots.sound: <musical brass and singing from the screen>

shots.camera: cut to Kuan in his seat, handheld camera close, physical move
shots.action: Kuan squeezes his eyes shut and buries his face in Dad's green cardigan; Dad pats his back
shots.space: Kuan left, Dad right, red seats around them

shots.camera: cut to a medium close-up of Kuan peeking through his fingers
shots.action: Kuan slowly spreads two fingers and peeks at the screen; a small smile appears; the blue robot toy sits beside him
shots.space: Kuan center, screen glow on his face

narration.text: For a long time, Kuan has been afraid to see films.
He would just close his eyes and bury his head into Dad's chest whenever anything scary appeared on the screen.
He's braver now and only covers his eyes a little.

transition_out.note: the eye reflection becomes the arcade screen glow

chunks.scene_note: Bright lobby with an arcade machine, candy counter, popcorn machine, and colorful snacks. Every screen, wrapper, and sign is blank: no letters, no numbers, no logos.

shots.camera: close-up of Kuan's eye, then a hard cut to a wide lobby shot; camera tracks right at walking pace
shots.action: Kuan's eye fills the frame; hard cut to the bright lobby; Kuan and Dad walk past the arcade, whose screen faces away and stays blank; Kuan points toward the popcorn machine

shots.camera: cut to a medium shot of Kuan at the candy counter, camera holds
shots.action: Kuan points at the candy jars; all packaging faces away from the camera and stays blank; Dad smiles beside him
shots.space: counter fills the frame, Kuan's reflection in the glass

shots.camera: cut to the popcorn machine, camera moves in physically with parallax
shots.action: popcorn bursts out of the machine and spills over the rim of a red-and-white tub toward the lens
shots.space: popcorn fills the foreground and then the whole frame

narration.text: The cinema has lots of video games, bright lights, and a huge place to buy candies and snacks.
I think the food is my favourite part of going to the cinema.
There's popcorn, chips, and sugar on everything.

transition_out.element: overflowing popcorn from the red-and-white tub
transition_out.note: the popcorn clears to the counter

chunks.scene_note: At the counter, the narrator asks who should buy popcorn. Dad says Kuan can buy it. Kuan and the narrator use their saved money.

shots.camera: medium shot at the counter, camera holds and follows Dad's hand
shots.action: Dad leans on the counter and looks at Kuan; Kuan holds the popcorn tub up hopefully
shots.space: Dad left, Kuan right, counter between them

shots.camera: cut to a close-up of a hand opening, coins in the palm
shots.action: Kuan pours coins into the narrator's palm; the coins catch the light; the two small hands count them
shots.space: hands fill the frame, counter blurred behind

shots.camera: cut to the snack bag being filled, camera tracks the bag
shots.action: the snack seller drops snacks into a plain paper bag with no labels; Kuan reaches for it; one coin spins on the counter and fills the frame
shots.space: the spinning coin becomes the whole frame

narration.text: Who should buy popcorn? I say, interested to see if Dad gets the hint.
Kuan and I have saved some money this week for a new toy.
Still, snacks would be nice. Kuan and I decide to use our money and buy some snacks before the film begins.

transition_out.note: the coin lands in a palm, then the auditorium lights dim

chunks.scene_note: They settle into their seats with snacks; the crowd goes quiet; the film starts. Kuan is nervous, then the film has talking cars and a karate car.

shots.camera: wide shot from behind the seats, camera tracks slowly down the row
shots.action: Kuan and Dad settle into their seats; Kuan puts the popcorn tub on his lap; the lights dim row by row
shots.space: rows of red seats, screen glowing ahead

shots.camera: cut to a close-up of Kuan's face lit by the screen
shots.action: Kuan grips the armrest, eyes wide; he takes a breath and leans forward
shots.space: screen light flickers on his face

shots.camera: cut to the screen: a car with a karate pose, then a car headlight fills the frame
shots.action: the film car spins and kicks; its headlight flares and fills the frame
shots.space: film world only inside the screen

narration.text: We bring our snacks to the cinema, the crowd gets quiet, and the film comes on the screen.
I always get a little nervous before the film starts.
This film has cars that talk, my favourite actor, and a car that knows karate.
In other words it has all of the parts of a great film.

transition_out.element: the film car's headlight becoming a warm table lamp
transition_out.note: the headlight fades into the dinner-table lamp

chunks.scene_note: At home, Kuan and the narrator laugh about the film at the dinner table; Dad is already snoring.

shots.camera: medium two-shot at the table, camera slowly tracks around the table
shots.action: Kuan acts out a karate kick with his arms; Dad leans back in his chair, eyes closed, snoring softly

shots.camera: cut to Kuan laughing, handheld, physical move
shots.action: Kuan laughs out loud and nearly spills his drink; he points at Dad and covers his mouth

shots.camera: cut to a wide shot of the table, camera holds still
shots.action: the lamp dims; Dad's head nods; Kuan leans on the table and smiles; the frame gently settles
shots.space: whole table in frame, warm evening light

narration.text: Kuan and I are laughing out loud! We have got to see it again.
We'll be talking about the film at the dinner table for a week.
Dad will not be. He's snoring.

transition_out.element: the warm lamp light bleeding into the paper texture
